title: The show window budget charges readers for pretty-printed JSON nobody receives
outcome: A record window fits as many rows as the reader will actually be sent, so paging a long history costs the round trips the delivered bytes justify rather than the bytes of a rendering no consumer sees
acceptance: A fixture with realistic multi-kilobyte note bodies shows more rows per page after the change than before, with the page boundary still identical between the JSON and text surfaces

The fit decision measures the bytes each surface actually delivers: compact structured JSON for MCP callers and rendered text for text mode; pretty-printed JSON is never the measure unless it is what the caller receives

completion.summary: Show windows fit compact JSON and rendered text, never pretty JSON, and keep identical row counts across surfaces.
